Status workflow with a readable history: a purchase request starts `submitted`; a `manager` approves or rejects it and marks an approved one ordered (a `when:` condition allows it only up to an amount); its requester may withdraw it. Nobody writes the status column directly, and everyone who may read a request may read who changed it and when.

content:
# Status workflow: a purchase request moves submitted -> approved or rejected
# (a manager decides) or withdrawn (the requester), and everyone who may read
# a request may read its history.
site_name: "Purchase requests"
auth:
  identifier: email
versioned: [requests]               # keeps every state a change replaced: the history
access:
  requests:
    read: owner_or_role:manager     # the requester; every request for a manager
    write: everyone
    update: owner_or_role:manager   # a transition is an update of the row
    delete: admin

model Request {
  id          Int      @id @default(autoincrement())
  title       String
  amountCents Int      @map("amount_cents")
  status      String   @default("submitted")     // moved only by workflows.yaml
  userId      Int      @map("user_id")
  createdAt   DateTime @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  updatedAt   DateTime @default(now()) @updatedAt @map("updated_at")
  @@map("requests")
}

# workflows.yaml - the only way a request's status changes
requests:
  table: requests
  field: status
  initial: submitted
  transitions:
    submitted:
      approved:  { role: manager }
      rejected:  { role: manager }
      withdrawn: {}                 # no role: whoever may update the row, here its requester
    approved:
      ordered:   { role: manager, when: "amount_cents <= 500000" }

check: A create starts in `submitted` whatever it sends. GET /api/requests/<id>/transitions answers {current, transitions} with only the moves the caller may make. POST /api/requests/<id>/transition {to} answers 200 {status:'transitioned', from, to}; without the role 403 `role 'manager' required for this transition`; with an unmet `when:` 422 `condition not met`; from a final state 409 {error:'no transitions from current state'}. A PATCH that sends `status` changes the other fields and names it in X-Stripped-Fields. GET /api/requests/<id>/versions lists one entry per change (`_version`, `_changed_by`, `_valid_from`, `_valid_to`), and /versions/<n> shows the row as it was; another member gets 404 on the request, its history and its transitions.
notes: A transition is an update: the caller needs the table's `update` rule and row scope as well as the transition's role, which is why `update` is `owner_or_role:manager` (`workflows.transition_writes`).
`manager` is the account's own role here; in a multi-tenant app a transition role also matches the member's role in the current tenant (`workflows.transition_roles`).
`versioned:` gives the history to the people who may read the row. Every transition is also in the admin's audit log (GET /api/_audit, action `transition`).
Give the state column the same `@default` as `initial:`; a different one is refused when the file is written (`workflows.create_null_state`).
